_readme: Settings for the automated blog pipeline (scripts/blog-quality-check.js + the 'daily-blog-carpetcleaningservice' scheduled task). Mirrors the pattern used by the rvfitfinder-site content engine, adapted for a flat static-HTML site with no build step.
cadenceDecisionNote: User originally asked for 2/day fully automated. Web research (2026-08-19) showed this risks Google's scaled-content-abuse detection, especially right after this site added 111 templated location pages in the same session, and contradicts this project's own seo/content-strategy.md (guides deliberately capped at 14, not 40+, to avoid padding). Recommended 3x/week; user settled on 1/day as the final decision. See seo/blog-topic-backlog.md decision log.
autoDeployNote: 2026-08-19: site is now live at carpetcleaningservice.ie (Netlify, DNS pending propagation) and the GitHub repo (MissBlack22/carpetcleaningservice-ie) is connected to Netlify's continuous deployment — every push to main auto-deploys live. User explicitly asked for automatic deploy. The daily blog routine (RemoteTrigger cloud job) still never runs a deploy command itself — pushing to GitHub is now sufficient, Netlify's own git integration handles the rest.
heroImagePolicy: Every post must use ONE real photo from assets/photos/business/ (or assets/photos/business/equipment/) placed right after the lead paragraph, plus the same path in og:image. Never a stock photo, never an AI-generated image, never a placeholder. Run `find assets/photos/business -name '*.webp' -not -name '*-800.webp'` to see the current real-photo library and pick whichever genuinely fits the post's specific topic (e.g. a mattress photo for a mattress post, a rug photo for a rug post) rather than defaulting to the same carpet photo every time. If truly nothing in the library fits the topic, use the closest reasonable match rather than skipping the image or inventing one.
bannedContentPatterns: fabricated prices or cost figures not sourced from carpet-cleaning-prices-dublin/
customer testimonials, reviews, or star ratings
invented statistics without a cited real source found via WebSearch
